problems.explain: With a₁ = 7 and d = 1, Sₙ = n(2a₁ + (n − 1)d)/2 = n(14 + 1(n − 1))/2 = 385. Multiplied out, n² + 13n − 770 = 0, whose roots are n = 22 and n = −35. A count of terms cannot be negative. So 22 terms add up to 385.

prompt.v: How many terms of the arithmetic series 7 + 9 + 11 + … add up to 112?

problems.explain: With a₁ = 7 and d = 2, Sₙ = n(2a₁ + (n − 1)d)/2 = n(14 + 2(n − 1))/2 = 112. Multiplied out, 2n² + 12n − 224 = 0, whose roots are n = 8 and n = −14. A count of terms cannot be negative. So 8 terms add up to 112.

problems.explain: With a₁ = 8 and d = 1, Sₙ = n(2a₁ + (n − 1)d)/2 = n(16 + 1(n − 1))/2 = 248. Multiplied out, n² + 15n − 496 = 0, whose roots are n = 16 and n = −31. A count of terms cannot be negative. So 16 terms add up to 248.
